claims.claim: The two explicit contribution bullets frame statistical characterization of GAN/diffusion imagery and differentiating DCT traces as the primary work. Coefficient distributions and JPEG persistence are the studied objects, rather than incidental detector ablations.
Experiments compare three broad image classes, standard classifiers and manual/LIME subsets of63AC statistics, followed by JPEG quality factors90/70/50/30.

caveats: Manuscript v3 is not asserted publisher-final equivalent; no scientific evidence is silently borrowed from a later work.

§3 prose gives72334total images and19334real,37572GAN,15423DM; their sum is72329. Table1 instead gives19341real, and its displayed GAN architecture rows sum37572 while its DM rows sum15423, yielding72336overall. Neither sum equals72334; no correction is applied.

§4.3 averages LIME contributions over correctly classified test images; a separate selection/evaluation split is not established in the inspected text, so test-informed feature-selection optimism remains a validity concern.
The three prediction classes are real/GAN-family/DM-family; this review does not change current tasks or equate broad family recognition with individual generator attribution.
Figure5 caption says high frequencies vanish as QF increases, while §5.2 correctly discusses stronger compression as QF decreases. Preserve the caption/text inconsistency.

Table2 shows all-coefficient GradientBoosting RAW82.57% versus POS-LIME82.21%; do not restate LIME as uniformly superior. Correlations, classification accuracy and LIME importance do not establish unique universally causal fingerprints.
